title: billing-blame-assignment-service-per-route-model-customer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a dedicated backend service (Billing Blame Assignment Service, BBAS) that computes per-request and aggregated cost and latency breakdowns attributed to route, model variant, and customer. BBAS will reconcile telemetry (request traces, kernel timings, batching metadata, and cache events) into an explainable, auditable ledger used by Console for per-route/model/customer cost views and by billing pipelines for chargeback. The focus is: (1) handle inference-level complexities like batching and KV-cache prefix hits, (2) attribute marginal cost for multi-tenant shared pools, and (3) provide deterministic, reproducible outputs for audit and dispute resolution.
technical_design: Architecture: streaming consumer reads enriched traces from kafka://telemetry-enriched (per-request spans, model exec metadata, GPU op durations). Enrichment upstream tags each token with model_variant,kernel_id,seq_len,batch_pos,kv_cache_hit:true|false. BBAS reconstructs per-request execution timeline, then applies an attribution engine with two stages: deterministic decomposition (kernel-time-to-token heuristics, prefix-crediting rules) and a learned marginality estimator (LightGBM model trained on synthetic microbenchmarks to predict per-request marginal GPU-ms under varying batch shapes). Outputs: 1) per-request attribution record (token_count, attributed_gpu_ms, attributed_memory_bytes, attributed_cost_usd, latency_breakdown) 2) daily rollups into ClickHouse for Console queries and chargeback export. Idempotency & dedup: use request_id + trace_id hashing and once-only watermarking. Backfill strategy: incremental replays via consumer groups with checkpointing. Scaling: horizontally stateless consumers with sharded state for in-flight batch reconstructions; use Redis for small hot lookups (model profiles) and S3 for large historical traces. Privacy: scrub prompt text; store only hashed prompt signatures when needed. Audit: every attribution record stores the version of attribution model and deterministic rule set (as strings) so later replays use exact code/weights.
migration_plan: Phase 0: implement service in shadow mode; subscribe to telemetry-enriched topic and write attributions to a staging ClickHouse table. Phase 1 (2w): run in parity mode comparing current aggregate rollups vs BBAS outputs; collect diff metrics, surface in Grafana. Phase 2 (1w): incremental rollout to Console read-views for a subset of tenant orgs (beta flag) and allow manual reconciliation step. Phase 3: cutover and enable chargeback export when parity metrics are within thresholds. Backfill: run backfill job for last 90 days to populate historic views for top-100 customers to validate billing reconciliation. Contingency: rollback to legacy aggregator and freeze billing exports for contested periods.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic benchmark accuracy: BBAS attributed per-request cost within 5% of ground-truth microbenchmarks across batch shapes and seq-lens
Shadow parity: aggregate monthly cost per-customer deviates <3% vs current ledger for top-50 tenants after 2-week shadow run
Latency SLA: end-to-end nearline attribution processing latency under 200ms p95 for streaming path (not including heavy backfills)
Observability: Grafana dashboards for attribution drift, per-model bias, and per-tenant disagreement with legacy accounting
Traceability: every attribution stored with attribution_version tag and a reproducible audit replay succeeds for 30-day window
comments: 2026-03-08 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff spike completed. Collected sample telemetry for dense batching scenarios; observed that kernel_time fields are present but missing kernel_id in ~1.2% of traces. Filing upstream fix with infra team.

2026-03-09 - Marco Liu: Design review with runtime team. Decided deterministic prefix-crediting rule: when kv_cache_hit=true for all tokens in prefix, attribute 0 token-cost for those tokens and attach a prefix_credit metadata to final attribution. This avoids negative attributions seen in naive marginal estimates.

2026-03-10 - Marco Liu: Implemented initial consumer prototype and synthetic data generator. Ran microbenchmarks: learned marginal estimator reduces noise vs pure heuristics on variable batch sizes (RMSE down 27%). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-attributor/pull/1234

2026-03-11 - Design feedback from PM (Olivia Chen): include explicit reconciliation window and UI-facing confidence score per-tenant in Console. Added 'confidence' float to output schema (will be stringified for ledger storage).

2026-03-12 - Reliability note (SRE - Jamal Rivera): heavy backfills saturate ClickHouse ingest. We will rate-limit backfill jobs and use day-partitioned bulk writes. Added backoff logic to migration_plan.
2026-03-13 - Security review requested: ensure no PII in attribution records. Security suggested storing hashed tenant prompt signatures and rotating hashing salt. Action assigned to Marco.

Follow-ups: create a lightweight reconciliation tool that shows per-tenant diffs grouped by route/model; run customer validation with two pilot tenants (fintech and healthcare) before enabling chargeback exports.
